rationale: Extended the no-snapshot probe to execute the containment consequence that had only been derived from source: after each restart the harness now isolates the node from every peer for a second and records whether it ever became candidate or leader, how many servers its configuration holds, and the term before and after. Local construction feedback: the feature-enabled restart, whose configuration is empty, stayed a follower and never campaigned; the control restart, holding {A,B,C}, reached Candidate. Both kept their term, which is the pre-vote behaviour rather than a failure to campaign, so the term is recorded as an operand and not asserted.

scope.description: The two restart modes of the no-snapshot fixture, each followed by isolating the restarted node from its peers for one second to see whether a node with an empty configuration campaigns.
assumptions: The isolation is expressed by disconnecting the restarted node from every peer, so it hears no heartbeat and its heartbeat timer fires within the observation window (the configured heartbeat timeout is 50ms and the window is one second).
The observation is a sample of the node's state every 5ms; campaigning is recorded as observed if the state was ever candidate or leader during the window.
The term is recorded as an operand: with pre-vote active a candidate does not increment its term until a pre-vote succeeds, so the term is not used as a predicate.
The empty configuration and the bootstrap configuration come from the same restart events recorded in the previous receipt; this experiment repeats them so its own receipt carries the operands.
excluded: No votes are solicited from real peers, so this does not execute an election outcome for either mode.
No snapshot failure or crash is injected.

experiment.prefix: The harness builds three in-memory transports in a full mesh with per-node in-memory stores, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, starts the three nodes with MockFSM, elects B as leader, applies ten commands, takes no snapshot on A and emits a 'fixture' event. It then shuts A down and restarts it twice from its own stores, once with the feature enabled and once without it, emitting 'restart_with_feature' and 'restart_without_feature' with the returned flag, state, last applied index, reported configuration and its length. Immediately after each restart the harness disconnects A from B and C, samples A's state every 5ms for one second, and emits '<name>_isolated' with the configured server count, whether candidate or leader state was ever observed, whether the term advanced, the term before and after, and the final state. All nodes are shut down afterwards. Event order: fixture, restart_with_feature, restart_with_feature_isolated, restart_without_feature, restart_without_feature_isolated.
semantic_changes: After each restart the harness disconnects the restarted node from every peer, samples its state for one second, and emits an '<name>_isolated' event with the configured server count, whether campaigning was observed, the term before and after, and the final state.
Four comparisons are added over the two isolated events.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft follower election gate and the pre-vote extension: the gate refuses to campaign while the latest configuration index is zero, and a campaigning node runs a pre-vote before incrementing its term.

comparisons.description: Feature on: the restarted node's configuration should be empty, so the isolation is exercised against that state.
Feature on: an isolated node whose configuration is empty should not campaign, keeping the consequence contained.
Feature off control: the same isolation applied to a node holding the bootstrap membership.
Feature off control: with a configuration the isolated node should campaign, so the isolation is a real trigger.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds an isolation phase after each restart so the containment consequence is executed instead of derived from source: the node is cut off from every peer for one second and sampled for campaigning, configuration size and term movement. The earlier comparisons are unchanged and remain with their own receipt.
